title: Give intermediate and advanced a reply-shape router
description:
COS-18 measured D3 — no statement of which shape a reply should take — on both files, and it is the cleanest of the four defects it found.

Run `2026-08-20T12-12-10-010Z`, 600 cells, 0 errored:

| style / model | D3 violations | share | on non-status cases |
|---|---|---|---|
| intermediate / sonnet | 47 | 16.2% | 47 (100%) |
| intermediate / opus | 39 | 11.8% | 39 (100%) |
| advanced / sonnet | 30 | 10.1% | 30 (100%) |
| advanced / opus | 22 | 8.3% | 22 (100%) |

All 138 land on non-status cases. Not one lands on a status update. The judge names the mechanism without being asked: 'the guide's status-update format is the only structure defined, and the reply instead reads as a lecture'.

Both files offer four shapes — status update, long-session report, decision, tie-break — and neither says which a given reply should take. COS-16 gave beginner `## Pick the shape from the question` (`plain-english-beginner.md:27-36`) for exactly this.

Two traps for whoever takes it.

**A router adds a rule.** COS-16 found that every regression it measured came from an edit that added rather than removed or bounded one, and its four-edit bundle showed an Opus reply-length regression that none of its parts showed alone. Measure the router by itself.

**Do not copy beginner's router's pre-fix placement.** COS-29 is resolved (session 38): the precedence sentence used to sit after the section's closing line, giving it that line — not the four bullets — as its nearest plural antecedent. It now sits directly under the four router bullets, above 'The shape changes with the question. The size never does.' Copy that placement, verbatim in spirit, when writing this router's own precedence sentence.

Advanced needs one extra thing intermediate does not: `plain-english-advanced.md:34` says 'Beat 3 always appears', making one status beat unconditional in a file that never says when the status shape applies. A router has to say whether 'always' survives outside a status update.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Each file's router is measured on its own, not bundled with any other edit, at n >= 146 non-errored cells per model on the five shared cases
The D3 violation share is re-counted after the change with the same classifier COS-18 used, and the before/after counts are recorded
Advanced's 'Beat 3 always appears' is either scoped to status updates or deliberately left unconditional with the reason recorded
No paired interval on rules, judge, composite or words is negative and clear of zero for either style
Validated on the reserve split for each style whose text changes
The precedence wording does not reproduce COS-29's dangling antecedent

plan:
1. Author one router edit per file (## Pick the shape from the question), mirroring beginner's COS-29-fixed structure: bullets map only to the shapes each file actually defines (status-update/three-questions, decision) since neither file has beginner's 'why'/'what-is' shapes; precedence sentence sits directly under the bullets, before 'The shape changes / size never does' line. Advanced's 'Beat 3 always appears' left unconditional -- the router now scopes 'always' to the status-update shape by section-adjacency, so no second edit needed (avoids bundling per COS-16's lesson).
2. Probe 2 cells per style, then measure each router on its own: 150 cells/model (30 repeats), shared five cases, WITH judge scoring this time (AC #4 requires judge+composite, unlike COS-29/30's --no-judge arms).
3. Paired interval (rules, judge, composite, words) per style against the COS-18 baseline (2026-08-20T12-12-10-010Z, filtered to the relevant style) -- AC #4 fails only if any metric is negative AND clear of zero.
4. Recount D3 violations post-change against the same judgeViolation-text classification method COS-18 used (no saved script existed; write one, document the method) -- AC #2.
5. Reserve-split validation per style (6 reserve-* cases) -- AC #5.
6. Record the Beat-3 decision explicitly -- AC #3.
implementationNotes:
Advanced: measured, not shipped. Router text (verbatim, as measured; kept here because the intermediate router's text was lost uncommitted between sessions):
## Pick the shape from the question

- You finished a job, or they asked how it went — use the three beats below.
- They asked you to choose between options — use the decision shape.
- They asked why something happens, or what something is or does — answer that directly. Do not force the three beats or the decision shape onto it.

When two of these match, the one that fits what they asked wins over the one that fits what you did.

The shape changes with the question. The size never does.

Shared five, router run 2026-08-31T20-45-10-304Z (150/model, 0 errored) vs COS-18 baseline 2026-08-20T12-12-10-010Z filtered to advanced, paired 95% t, n=10 pairs: rules -0.4 [-1.1,+0.4], judge -0.0 [-4.5,+4.5], composite -0.3 [-1.9,+1.3], words +1.9 [-4.3,+8.1]. Reserve, router 2026-09-05T12-27-22-593Z vs baseline 2026-09-05T12-41-42-888Z (both 150/model, 0 errored), n=12 pairs: rules -0.1 [-0.7,+0.5], judge +2.3 [-4.2,+8.9], composite +0.6 [-1.6,+2.8], words +2.5 [-2.6,+7.5]. No interval negative and clear of zero.

D3 recount (harness/scratchpad/d3-classify.mjs, a reconstruction of COS-18's lost classifier; trust direction over absolute level; all hits fall on the three non-status cases): opus 38 -> 47, sonnet 46 -> 43 violations per 150 rows. The router does not reduce D3 on advanced. Shipping it would add a rule with no measured benefit, the risk COS-16 names, so the file keeps no router.

AC #3 (Beat 3): left unconditional. With no router in advanced, 'always' still sits inside the status-update section it governs, so there is nothing to re-scope.

Which runs carried a router was inferred from the router's own phrases ('Pick the shape', 'The shape changes with the question') appearing in judge text: present in 20-35/20-45/12-14/12-27, absent from 12-41/13-02 and from COS-18's baseline. Rows do not store the style text.

Intermediate: the router measured in 2026-08-31T20-35-40-401Z (shared five) and 2026-09-05T12-14-25-448Z (reserve) was never committed and is lost; no session log or results row holds its text. Rebuilt 2026-10-05 from the judge's verbatim quotes of it in those runs ('Pick the shape from the question', 'You finished a job, or they asked how it went — use the three questions below', 'they asked why something happens... answer that directly', 'The shape changes with the question. The size never does.'), which match advanced's router with 'three beats' -> 'three questions'. Because rebuilt text is not provably the measured text, it is re-measured from scratch; the two runs above are evidence of direction only. D3 under the lost version, same classifier: opus 81 -> 61, sonnet 92 -> 49 per 150 rows vs COS-18. Rebuilt text (placed under '## Intermediate level', above the three questions):
## Pick the shape from the question

- You finished a job, or they asked how it went — use the three questions below.
- They asked you to choose between options — use the decision shape.
- They asked why something happens, or what something is or does — answer that directly. Do not force the three questions or the decision shape onto it.

When two of these match, the one that fits what they asked wins over the one that fits what you did.

The shape changes with the question. The size never does.

Intermediate, rebuilt router, shared five: run 2026-10-05T18-43-33-821Z, 150/model, 0 errored, all judged (AC #1). Paired 95% t vs COS-18 baseline 2026-08-20T12-12-10-010Z filtered to intermediate, n=10 pairs: rules -0.0 [-0.6,+0.5], judge +4.5 [+0.8,+8.2], composite +1.8 [+0.3,+3.3], words -2.6 [-6.3,+1.1]. No interval negative and clear of zero; judge and composite improve clear of zero (AC #4, shared five). D3 recount, same classifier on both sides (AC #2): opus 81 -> 52, sonnet 92 -> 50 violations per 150 rows, all on the three non-status cases (lost version: 61 / 49). Caveat: the baseline is six weeks older than the after-run, so part of the judge gain could be model drift rather than the router; the D3 drop is the router's own target and is consistent across both versions.

Next (session hit its usage limit here): (1) when 2026-10-05T19-04-48-633Z finishes (or if it stopped short), check its row/error counts; (2) commit nothing else to the style file until (3) the reserve baseline gap is filled: temporarily remove the router from plain-english-intermediate.md (text is committed on feature/COS-31), run 'node src/cli.mjs run --styles=plain-english-intermediate --variants=baseline --models=sonnet --cases=reserve-decision-tie,reserve-agentic-session --repeats=25', then restore the router with git checkout; (4) interval --before=results/2026-09-05T13-02-20-890Z/rows.json,<fill>/rows.json --after=results/2026-10-05T19-04-48-633Z/rows.json for rules/judge/composite/words (AC #4 reserve, AC #5); (5) tick ACs and finalize.

Intermediate, reserve (AC #4 reserve, AC #5): filled the before-side gap. 2026-09-05T13-02-20-890Z lost 43 sonnet rows to the monthly spend limit (all 25 reserve-decision-tie, 18 of 25 reserve-agentic-session) plus 1 opus max-turns error. Fill run 2026-10-05T21-50-08-914Z: pre-router file (byte-identical to 7d21c5a, the text 13-02 measured), sonnet, those two cases, 25 repeats, 50/50, 0 errored, all judged; router restored afterwards and the file matches HEAD. After-run 2026-10-05T19-04-48-633Z: 300/300, 0 errored. Errored rows dropped before pairing: the CLI's interval does not filter them and they carry scores (a spend-limit message scored judge 1.0). Paired 95% t, before = 13-02 non-errored + fill, n=12 pairs: rules +0.7 [-0.2,+1.7], judge +12.3 [+5.4,+19.2], composite +5.3 [+2.3,+8.4], words -3.7 [-13.2,+5.9]. Using the fill only for the two sonnet gap cases gives the same within 0.1. No interval negative and clear of zero. Drift caveat: per-pair judge deltas are +3.1 and -0.1 on the two same-day pairs (sonnet decision-tie and agentic-session vs the fill) but up to +31 on pairs against the Sep-05 baseline, so most of the judge gain is likely model drift. What is established is no regression plus the D3 drop on the shared five, not a judge improvement.

AC #2 left unchecked deliberately. Before/after D3 counts are recorded for both styles, but the criterion names 'the same classifier COS-18 used', and that classifier was never saved. harness/scratchpad/d3-classify.mjs is a reconstruction applied unchanged to both sides, so direction is trustworthy and absolute level is not. Tick it only if a reconstruction applied on both sides is accepted as meeting the criterion. AC #6 evidence: in 108b00b the precedence sentence sits directly under the three router bullets, above 'The shape changes with the question. The size never does.', so its nearest plural antecedent is the bullets, not the closing line (COS-29's defect).
finalSummary: Intermediate ships a '## Pick the shape from the question' router (108b00b). It is a rebuild of the router measured 2026-08-31, whose text was never committed, re-measured on its own. Advanced was measured with the same router and does not ship it: no D3 effect. Advanced's 'Beat 3 always appears' stays unconditional because, with no router, it still sits inside the status section it governs. Verified on intermediate, 150/model, 0 errored, paired 95% t. Shared five (2026-10-05T18-43-33-821Z vs COS-18 baseline): rules -0.0 [-0.6,+0.5], judge +4.5 [+0.8,+8.2], composite +1.8 [+0.3,+3.3], words -2.6 [-6.3,+1.1]; D3 on non-status cases opus 81->52, sonnet 92->50. Reserve (2026-10-05T19-04-48-633Z vs 2026-09-05T13-02-20-890Z, with the spend-limit gap filled by 2026-10-05T21-50-08-914Z and errored rows dropped): rules +0.7 [-0.2,+1.7], judge +12.3 [+5.4,+19.2], composite +5.3 [+2.3,+8.4], words -3.7 [-13.2,+5.9]. No interval is negative and clear of zero on either split. The judge gains are probably mostly model drift: same-day reserve pairs read +3.1 and -0.1. The established result is fewer shape violations with no regression. AC #2 stays unchecked: COS-18's classifier was lost, and a reconstruction was applied to both sides instead.
